These are preliminary maps derived from satellite radar and should be used as guidance only. Coloured pixels may include false positives, and their absence does not mean an absence of damage or flooding.
methodology_other: Change detection on synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite images acquired before and after the event. Damage Proxy Maps show significant changes in radar coherence and amplitude; Flood Proxy Maps show areas that changed to standing water. Maps are preliminary and checked against news reports and ground-level imagery where available.

# Philippines Typhoons Toraji Usagi Man-yi: Damage and Flood Proxy Maps, Nov 2024

The **Earth Observatory of Singapore – Remote Sensing Lab (EOS-RS)** produced these damage and flood proxy maps for Philippines Typhoons Toraji Usagi Man-yi (Nov 2024) from synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite images. Each map is a separate ZIP below with its GeoTIFF, a KMZ for Google Earth, the PNG figures and a text file describing how it was made and how to read it.

## Maps in this dataset

- **EOS-RS Damage Proxy Map: Isabela Province, Philippines, Typhoons Toraji, Usagi & Man-yi, 19 Nov 2024, v0.9**
- **EOS-RS Flood Proxy Map: Isabela Province, Philippines, Floods from Typhoons Toraji, Usagi & Man-yi, 19 Nov 2024, v0.9**

organization.description: The Earth Observatory of Singapore - Remote Sensing Lab (EOS-RS) is a research lab at Nanyang Technological University (NTU), Singapore. It uses satellite remote sensing, mainly synthetic aperture radar (SAR), to map natural hazards and disasters. The lab produces Damage Proxy Maps (DPMs) and Flood Proxy Maps (FPMs) showing where damage or flooding has likely occurred. Its work focuses on Southeast Asia and the wider Asia-Pacific, and it also responds to major disasters worldwide.

resources.description:
EOS-RS Damage Proxy Map: Isabela Province, Philippines, Typhoons Toraji, Usagi & Man-yi, 19 Nov 2024, v0.9

ZIP containing: GeoTIFF, KMZ, PNG, TXT.

The Earth Observatory of Singapore - Remote Sensing Lab (EOS-RS) created this preliminary Damage Proxy Map (DPM) depicting areas that are likely damaged in the Province of Isabela, Philippines, following Typhoons Toraji, Usagi, and Man-yi in November 2024. This map was derived from synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images acquired by the Copernicus Sentinel-1 satellite operated by the European Space Agency (ESA) before (17 Feb 2024 to 11 May 2024) and after (19 Nov 2024) the event.

ZIP containing: GeoTIFF, KMZ, PNG, TXT, Shapefile.

The Earth Observatory of Singapore - Remote Sensing Lab (EOS-RS) created this preliminary Flood Proxy Map (FPM) depicting areas that are likely flooded in the Province of Isabela, Philippines, due to heavy rainfall from Typhoons Toraji, Usagi, and Man-yi in Nov 2024. This map was derived from synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images acquired by the Copernicus Sentinel-1 satellite operated by the European Space Agency (ESA) before (17 Feb 2024 to 11 May 2024) and after (19 Nov 2024) the event.
